risks: Unannounced simulations on working wards could distract staff from real patients, cause anxiety or be mistaken for real emergencies; interviews may touch on distressing calls.
consent: Rapid response team members and ward managers consent to the programme in advance and may opt out of being observed; ward nurses are told a simulation may occur on their ward in a given week; manikins are used, never patients; interviews need written consent; families are approached after the patient has stabilised, with interpreters.
data: Call records are abstracted with study codes; recordings of debriefs are made only with the team's consent and deleted after transcription.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients and families with limited English, patients on wards with fewer staff at night and patients in the smaller hospitals may benefit least. Scenarios include night-time and interpreter elements, results are reported by hospital size and time of day, and families with limited English are included in interviews with interpreters.
effectiveness: Success is a shorter time to first critical intervention with no harm from simulations and an explanation of hospital differences.
efficiency: Eight faculty hours a month per hospital and a grant of 48,000.
costs: About 21,000 for abstraction, 12,000 for transcription and interpreters, and 15,000 for faculty backfill.
grants: Grant SEF-2026-14; a larger authority-wide programme could seek provincial education funding.
partnerships: Education leads at the four hospitals, simulation faculty, rapid response teams, ward managers and a family partner from the patient and family advisory council.
rebPath: Application to the health authority research ethics board as board of record for the multi-site study; the decision is unknown and no simulation for research purposes or data abstraction begins before approval. Stop rules for real calls are part of the application.
limitations: Four hospitals; open programme delivery; call record timing may be imprecise.
summary: Safety rules and consent for unannounced simulation, equity reporting and a board of record decision still unknown.
